overview.tag: state as of today, counted from the repositories
overview.lede: Every number on this page comes from reading a repository or from the GitHub API, not from memory. Where something could not be verified, that is written out instead of filled in with a likely value.
substrates.tag: split by unit of work, not by stack
substrates.lede: The split does not follow the language or the framework, but what a given set of tools treats as the unit of work. That is the only criterion which predicts what can be shared: two projects on the same substrate can share a store, share scoring and share replay — two on different substrates can share nothing.
kernels.tag: hover to see what they feed
kernels.lede: One codebase — yes. One product — no. A kernel lowers the cost of maintenance and is a channel to reach people; it is never a sales offer. 'A platform that can do six things' has no buyer, because it answers no specific pain.
kernels.lede1: Components that tempt you to pull them out, and whose extraction would end in a library with one user or with the domain dragged inside. Each one names the type that holds it.
dups.lede: Pairs where the same problem was solved twice — because it lives in two different repositories and nobody stood in the place from which both are visible at once.
boundaries.lede: Gluing two substrates together gives a product that cannot be described in one sentence — and a product that cannot be described in one sentence has no buyer.
product.tag: where the open / paid line runs
distribution.lede: Every open artefact feeds one channel, which reaches one buyer, who buys one product. The order of the rows is the order they start in, not the order of importance.
principles.tag: a system, not a list of good intentions
principles.lede: Thirty-five repositories, one person, evenings and weekends. The bottleneck is not writing code — agents write it faster than it can be read. The bottleneck is attention and decision, so the whole system below optimises one quantity: how many decisions have to be taken to keep the portfolio from rotting.
tiers.lede: A repository with no declared level of service gets attention when you happen to think of it — that is, at random, and in practice once it has already broken. The tier is a promise made to yourself and the only thing that lets you deliberately not deal with twenty repositories in a given week.
cadence.lede: A ritual with no artefact at the end of it is a meeting with yourself. Each one below has one thing that stays in the repository afterwards — and that thing, not the feeling of having done something, is the evidence that it happened.
health.lede: This section only appears once scripts/collect-health.mjs has written data/health.json. Until it is there, the operating model next to it describes what should be measured — not what was measured.
checks.lede: A measure with no threshold is a chart, and a threshold with no written-down action is a pang of conscience. Every row below has all three parts, so that a breach ends in an action rather than a worry.
wip.lede: A one-person portfolio does not die from a lack of ideas. It dies from thirty-five things started and none finished. The limits below are hard: breaching them is a signal to close something, not to work longer.
automation.lede: Everything below exists to take a decision off a person, or to put it in front of them at the moment it can be taken in a minute. Each one names a path in the repository — if there is none, the automation is still to be built, and that is part of the plan.
plan.lede: Every horizon has a 'done when' test that can be checked without argument. A goal with no such test slides forever, because there is always one more thing that could be done.
index.tag: click a row to open the full description
index.lede: The full list with links, attention tier and state. The columns sort; a row opens a panel with the numbers, components, gaps and next steps.
glossary.tag: definitions of every term on the map
glossary.lede: Every term with a dotted underline on this page has its full definition here, together with the place it occurs in the portfolio.
rejected.tag: looks like a kernel, is not one
filter.search: Search a repository, a stack, a description…
check.action: what you do on a breach
drawer.privatelink: The repository is private — the link will work only once it is opened
footer.line: One codebase — yes. One product — no.
footer.fine: A kernel is a library with one claim in its README, never a sales offer. A platform is the consequence of having sold two products, not a precondition. This page is static and reads one file — data/portfolio.json; changing the portfolio means changing that file, and CI rejects a manifest that has stopped matching reality.
